sections.browser:
<browser>
You control one remote browser:
- snapshot: the active page's accessibility tree, with bracketed element IDs for run actions.
- run: snapshot actions by ID, or JavaScript against the Playwright-shaped page API. Pass exactly one of code or actions; every action uses "op" and "id", never "kind" or "ref".
- screenshot: the rendered page as an image.
- browser_read: the current page's content, filed as evidence with its URL.
- browser_relaunch: a fresh session, Verified or egressing from a given place.
- browser_release: release the session when you are done browsing.

Snapshot IDs are valid only for the latest snapshot of the active page; snapshot again after navigation or a stale ID. Use snapshot actions for single clicks and fills, and one run code call for a multi-step workflow that returns only the values you need. Do not launch another browser; open more tabs with context.newPage() inside run code.

The `run` page is Playwright-shaped, not Playwright. On this browser these throw: `page.waitForEvent("download")`, `page.route`, `page.waitForResponse`, `context.newCDPSession`, and `page.on` for `pageerror`, `framenavigated` or `response`. Wait for what the page shows instead (`page.waitForSelector`, `page.waitForLoadState`, or poll `page.url()` or a locator's text in a short loop), read results from the page itself (a locator's text, then `browser_read` to cite it), and never intercept or rewrite requests. A file the page offers as a download cannot be collected from the browser: take the link's URL from the page and fetch it with `web_fetch` when that tool is offered, or cite the page that links it.

After a click that loads a new page, wait for the next page with a bounded wait before reading it (for example `await page.waitForSelector("#result", { timeout: 1000 })`), and if a read made while the page was changing throws "Inspected target navigated or closed" or "Cannot find context with specified id", run that read once more: it is a read, so repeating it is safe.

Readers and actors: snapshot, screenshot and browser_read only read the page, and a read cut by an interruption runs again by itself. run acts on the site, so a run cut by an interruption is never repeated for you: you are told it was interrupted and on which page, and you check the page before acting again.

The browser is remote. It is launched on your first browser call and released when you call browser_release, after 180 seconds without a browser call, or when your work ends; the call after a release opens a fresh session with no cookies or page state.

Evidence: browser_read and screenshot are citable, filed with the page URL. snapshot and run return values are working views, not evidence.

Never repeat a failing call unchanged: the third identical call that failed the same way is refused. Change the code, the IDs (snapshot again), the URL or the approach.
</browser>
sections.task: Read the company's registry page in the browser and its filing scan, filing.png, in the workspace. Answer when it was incorporated, citing both.

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a text file. Output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete. Video files (mp4, webm, mov, mkv) come back as the video, or as the from_s..to_s window of it; pass `ask` with any image, video or PDF page to have a question about it answered. A browser session's recording listed as `session:<id>` is read the same way: `ask` (and a from_s..to_s window) is answered from what the recording shows. PDFs and office documents (docx, pptx, odt and the like) read as their extracted text, paged like any file; `page` reads one page. A page with no text layer (a scan), or a read with `ask`, renders the page (default 1) and looks at it. Spreadsheets are read with bash (the read says how). Every look is filed under evidence/ and is citable. A directory reads as a listing of its entries.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

ask.description: A question about what the image, video, video window or document page shows. The answer comes back with the media; a route that cannot see the media is answered by the harness's eyes.

from_s.description: Video only: start of the window to look at, in seconds.

to_s.description: Video only: end of the window to look at, in seconds (must be greater than from_s).

page.description: PDF or office document only: the page to read (1-based). Its text comes back; a page with no text layer, or a page read with ask, is rendered and looked at.

char_offset.description: Characters to skip at the start of the `offset` line (0-based). A line longer than the read limit comes back in consecutive windows; continue with the offset and char_offset each window names.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns combined stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: snapshot
toolsAdded.description: Capture the active page's Stagehand accessibility tree and hydrate its displayed IDs for subsequent run actions. Every call replaces the active page's ID map.

toolsAdded.name: run
toolsAdded.description: Browse and automate websites in the persistent Stagehand browser. Navigate with JavaScript such as await page.goto("https://example.com"); there is no separate navigate or start tool. Execute either a JavaScript workflow against the Stagehand Playwright facade or a batch of actions using IDs from the latest snapshot. Provide exactly one of code or actions. Each action must use "op" (never "kind") and "id" (never "ref"). Copy the bracketed snapshot ID as a string. Examples: {"actions":[{"op":"click","id":"1-42"}]}, {"actions":[{"op":"fill","id":"2-14","value":"Miami"}]}, {"actions":[{"op":"select","id":"3-9","values":"Lowest price"}]}.

actions.description: Snapshot actions with the exact fields "op" and "id". Do not use "kind" or "ref".

op.description: Action operation. Use "op": "click"; never use a "kind" field.

id.description: Bracketed ID copied from the latest snapshot, as a string. Use "id"; never use "ref".

op.description: Action operation. Use "op": "hover"; never use a "kind" field.

id.description: Bracketed ID copied from the latest snapshot, as a string. Use "id"; never use "ref".

id.description: Bracketed ID copied from the latest snapshot, as a string. Use "id"; never use "ref".

op.description: Action operation. Use "op": "type"; never use a "kind" field.

id.description: Bracketed ID copied from the latest snapshot, as a string. Use "id"; never use "ref".

op.description: Action operation. Use "op": "press"; never use a "kind" field.

id.description: Bracketed ID copied from the latest snapshot, as a string. Use "id"; never use "ref".

op.description: Action operation. Use "op": "select"; never use a "kind" field.

id.description: Bracketed ID copied from the latest snapshot, as a string. Use "id"; never use "ref".

toolsAdded.name: screenshot
toolsAdded.description: Capture a screenshot of the active page. For size-constrained MCP clients, prefer a viewport JPEG: {"type":"jpeg","quality":40,"fullPage":false}.

ask.description: What you want to know from this capture. Answered from the pixels when your model cannot see them; echoed back when it can.

toolsAdded.name: browser_read
toolsAdded.description: Read the CURRENT page of the browser as evidence and persist it under evidence/ with the page URL: `what` = markdown (the whole page as markdown, the default for citing), text, html, url, or title. This is the citable door for anything you saw in the browser: snapshot, screenshot and run return values are not evidence. Cite the returned URL.

toolsAdded.name: browser_release
toolsAdded.description: Release the browser session now. Call it as soon as you are done browsing for this task: an open session costs browser minutes whether or not you use it. Your next browser call launches a fresh session (a new tab, no cookies from the old one), so finish a flow before releasing.

toolsAdded.name: browser_relaunch
toolsAdded.description: Replace the browser session with a fresh one, after a site blocked it (403/429, a CAPTCHA wall, a bot-detection page, an empty page that should have content). The new session keeps the run's Verified setting unless `verified` names one: `verified: true` where the run's sessions are not Verified (a Verified browser carries a stronger identity and costs more). Use `geolocation` to browse as a visitor from a given place: the proxy egresses from that country (ISO alpha-2), optionally a US state and a city, so geo-aware sites (storefront region, prices, payment methods, content availability) show what a local sees. Page state is lost; navigate again with run.

verified.description: true launches the new session as a Verified browser, false as one that is not. Omitted, the new session keeps the run's setting.

geolocation.description: Proxy egress location for the new session. Omit to keep the run's default.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, e.g. GB, US, DE.

state.description: US state abbreviation, United States only.

city.description: City name, e.g. LONDON or SAO_PAULO.

toolsAdded.name: submit
toolsAdded.description: Deliver the record. It ends the run.

toolsAdded.name: screenshot
toolsAdded.description: Capture a screenshot of the active page. For size-constrained MCP clients, prefer a viewport JPEG: {"type":"jpeg","quality":40,"fullPage":false}.

ask.description: What you want to know from this capture. Answered from the pixels when your model cannot see them; echoed back when it can.

toolsAdded.name: browser_read
toolsAdded.description: Read the CURRENT page of the browser as evidence and persist it under evidence/ with the page URL: `what` = markdown (the whole page as markdown, the default for citing), text, html, url, or title. This is the citable door for anything you saw in the browser: snapshot, screenshot and run return values are not evidence. Cite the returned URL.

toolsAdded.name: browser_release
toolsAdded.description: Release the browser session now. Call it as soon as you are done browsing for this task: an open session costs browser minutes whether or not you use it. Your next browser call launches a fresh session (a new tab, no cookies from the old one), so finish a flow before releasing.

toolsAdded.name: browser_relaunch
toolsAdded.description: Replace the browser session with a fresh one, after a site blocked it (403/429, a CAPTCHA wall, a bot-detection page, an empty page that should have content). The new session keeps the run's Verified setting unless `verified` names one: `verified: true` where the run's sessions are not Verified (a Verified browser carries a stronger identity and costs more). Use `geolocation` to browse as a visitor from a given place: the proxy egresses from that country (ISO alpha-2), optionally a US state and a city, so geo-aware sites (storefront region, prices, payment methods, content availability) show what a local sees. Page state is lost; navigate again with run.

verified.description: true launches the new session as a Verified browser, false as one that is not. Omitted, the new session keeps the run's setting.

geolocation.description: Proxy egress location for the new session. Omit to keep the run's default.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, e.g. GB, US, DE.

state.description: US state abbreviation, United States only.

city.description: City name, e.g. LONDON or SAO_PAULO.

toolsAdded.name: submit
toolsAdded.description: Deliver the record. It ends the run.
